audit_findings.title: MatrixCare earnings are capitalized despite an imminent sale
audit_findings.magnitude: $220 million FY2026 revenue, $28 million operating profit including $28 million amortization, and $490 million gross announced proceeds
audit_findings.mechanism: Completion would remove MatrixCare owner earnings and add after-tax net proceeds to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2026, the MatrixCare business represented approximately $220 million of revenue and approximately $28 million of operating profit, which included approximately $28 million of amortization from acquired intangibles.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated valuation-date error. The supplied record still describes the sale as expected, so the AS_FILED perimeter correctly includes MatrixCare and excludes unreceived proceeds. Completion will make the current model stale, but the net valuation direction is mixed because both earnings and sale consideration change.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a filing confirming completion and closing adjustments, then rerun using post-sale owner earnings and after-tax net proceeds without estimating an unsupported carve-out.

audit_findings.title: Noctrix is fully owned but represented by only one month of results
audit_findings.mechanism: A full acquired-business claim is reflected in the balance sheet and cash outflow, while only one month of its operating earnings, working capital and maintenance investment enters anchor owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition has been accounted for as a business combination using purchase accounting and included in our consolidated financial statements from June 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but the record provides no full-year or run-rate Noctrix operating figures. The $335 million purchase price does not establish its recurring owner-earnings contribution, so neither direction nor materiality can be determined.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Noctrix run-rate revenue, operating costs, cash taxes, working-capital requirements and maintenance capital expenditure, then normalize the FY2026 owner-earnings anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Hedge liabilities may sit outside both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $217.807 million gross derivative liabilities, equal to approximately $1.49 per diluted valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economically uncovered derivative liability omitted from owner earnings would require a deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For net investment hedges that qualify and are designated for hedge accounting, the change in fair value of the derivative is recorded in cumulative translation adjustment within other comprehensive loss and reclassified into earnings when the hedged net investment is either sold or substantially liquidated.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether an uncovered liability exists is unresolved because the swaps hedge foreign net assets or intercompany debt. Even conservatively deducting all filed derivative liabilities, without credit for the $5.217 million derivative assets or hedged items, reduces value by only about $1.49 per share, versus the $12.42 per-share gap between the $228.35 price and $215.93 bull value. It therefore cannot change the stated valuation conclusion on the filed balance.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each derivative to its hedged item and expected settlement; rerun the bridge only if the reconciliation identifies an uncovered net economic liability.

audit_findings.title: The investment bridge uses accounting carrying amounts as value
audit_findings.magnitude: $160.739 million carrying amount: $80.579 million non-marketable, $76.801 million equity-method and $3.359 million marketable
audit_findings.mechanism: Replacing carrying amounts with after-tax realizable values changes the stakes component of the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Non-marketable equity securities are reported at cost, minus impairment, if any, plus or minus changes resulting from observable price changes in orderly transactions for the identical or similar investment of the same issuer.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation-basis concern is demonstrated, but misvaluation is only a possibility because no independent realizable values are supplied. The recorded bridge equals about $1.10 per diluted share and 0.6% of base equity value; a complete write-off alone would not change the conclusion, but the record does not establish the potential upside or disposal-tax adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Value each non-marketable and equity-method holding using current financing, operating or transaction evidence, estimate disposal taxes and liquidity discounts, and rerun the bridge with after-tax realizable values.

audit_findings.title: Expiring Singapore tax benefits are not explicitly normalized
audit_findings.magnitude: $37 million FY2026 net-income benefit; approximately $4.20 per share under the base capitalization multiple and $4.94 per share under the bull capitalization multiple if removed immediately and entirely
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration increases cash taxes and reduces forecast and terminal owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: A substantial portion of our manufacturing operations and administrative functions in Singapore operate under certain tax holidays and incentive programs that will expire in whole or in part at various dates through June 30, 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated because the benefits expire in whole or part through June 2030 while the model does not explicitly fade them. However, even the conservative computed case of immediately removing the entire $37 million recurring benefit reduces base value from $184.93 to about $180.73 and bull value from $215.93 to about $210.99, leaving both below the $228.35 price. Actual staged expiration would have a smaller present-value effect.
audit_findings.action: Map each incentive's expiry and extension conditions, model post-expiry cash taxes and Pillar Two interactions, and confirm that scenario growth rates are net of this headwind.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge predates a dividend already owed at the valuation date
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.66 per common share, approximately $95.2 million using 144.252306 million shares outstanding on August 10, or about $0.65 per diluted valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The declared dividend payable reduces cash attributable to the contemporaneous common-share claim and therefore reduces the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 6, 2026, our board of directors declared a cash dividend of $0.66 per common share, to be paid on September 24, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on August 20, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge-date error because the September 5 valuation adds June 30 cash after the August 20 record date without deducting the declared distribution. Its approximately $0.65-per-share effect is small relative to the $43.42 base-value shortfall and $12.42 bull-value shortfall versus market price, so it does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Roll the cash bridge forward to September 5, deduct the dividend payable using the exact record-date share count, incorporate other filed post-balance-sheet cash movements, and rerun per-share values.
